title: Runtime identity lock requirements v1
description: What the pinned patch series must keep carrying for a task to stay bound to the code it was admitted under. Each requirement is anchored to one line a named patch adds, because a check that parsed the TypeScript would be a second reading of a source the manifest already pins byte for byte.

id.description: Named so the contract can explain it and the validator can require that it does.

requires.description: What must hold, said as a property rather than as a line of code.

why.description: What goes wrong when it stops holding. A requirement whose cost nobody can state is one nobody will defend.

introduced_by.description: The patch that introduced the line, as the manifest names it. Provenance, not the scope of the check: the line is counted across the whole series in manifest order, because a guarantee introduced by one patch and deleted by a later one is a guarantee the code does not have.

added_line.description: One line the patch adds, verbatim and without its `+`. Anchoring to a line the patch adds means the requirement is met by bytes under the manifest's digest rather than by a pattern that happens to match.

occurrences.description: How many of this line the whole series leaves in place. A count rather than a presence test: a line that appears twice where one was expected is a copy someone made, and the requirement stops describing what it checks.

requirement_growth.description: The requirement-count budget: the count the document carries, the previous approved baseline, and the net delta the validator recomputes. Positive growth owes a rationale and the candidates considered for replacement or removal, because a requirement nobody can justify is how a lock becomes a list.

requirements.description: How many requirements the document carries. Recorded rather than recomputed at write time so that a set edited without resealing the budget is a disagreement, not a silent update.

previous_approved.description: The requirement count at the last approved sealing. The validator does not verify that provenance: what holds the baseline is the candidate pin — the lock is a design-candidate member, so raising it moves candidate_digest and goes before the panel.

net_delta.description: requirements minus previous_approved. Recorded so a reader sees the growth; recomputed by the validator so a recorded delta cannot lie.

growth_rationale.description: Why the set grew past baseline. Required whenever net_delta is positive.

replacement_candidates.description: Requirements considered for replacement or removal to absorb the growth. Required to be non-empty whenever net_delta is positive.

lock_digest.description: sha256 over this document with the field removed, so the requirement set is bound as a set.
